# rabbitmq

```go
import "github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/brokers/rabbitmq"
```

Package rabbitmq implements the blkit MessageBroker against RabbitMQ 3.13\+ (specs/message\-brokers/rabbitmq\-message\-broker.spec.md).

Mapping to primitives:

- Jobs ride quorum queues (one per ProcessKey) behind a topic exchange "\<prefix\>.jobs". Workers consume with manual ack and a bounded prefetch; terminal Report\* verbs and ReportSuspended ack the delivery. A worker whose channel closes has its unacked deliveries requeued by RabbitMQ immediately — that is the redelivery story (no timeout wait).
- Instance events ride a single RabbitMQ stream "\<prefix\>.inst\-events" shared by all instances (retention via x\-max\-age). Subscribers replay the stream from the start to reconstruct the latest lifecycle and terminal events, then follow live, filtering client\-side by the instance id carried in the message headers.
- The worker registry is a heartbeat broadcast on a fanout exchange "\<prefix\>.registry" (RabbitMQ has no KV): RegisterProcesses and Heartbeat publish the worker's full registration set, Unregister an explicit removal, and every broker handle maintains a local cache fed by a private auto\-delete queue, marking workers lost when no broadcast arrives within RegistrationTTL.
- Delayed resume uses the per\-message\-TTL \+ dead\-letter\-exchange pattern: the JobResume is published to a holding queue whose DLX is the jobs exchange, with the instance's routing key.
- Cancel of still\-queued jobs is unsupported natively (AMQP has no selective removal), so Cancel always takes the JobCancel route and the AllowExternalCancel opt\-in applies to every cancel.

## type [Broker](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L85-L110>)

Broker is the RabbitMQ MessageBroker backend. Create one with New; it satisfies both the producer\-side and worker\-side halves of bl.MessageBroker.

```go
type Broker struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L154>)

```go
func New(cfg Config) (*Broker, error)
```

New connects to RabbitMQ, declares the exchanges, the delay queue, the instance\-event stream, and this handle's private registry queue, and starts the registry consumer and sweeper. Release resources with Close.

<a name="Broker.Cancel"></a>
### func (\*Broker) [Cancel](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L753>)

```go
func (b *Broker) Cancel(ctx context.Context, req bl.CancelRequest) error
```

Cancel always takes the JobCancel route: AMQP cannot selectively remove a queued message, so the overview's best\-effort queue removal is skipped and the AllowExternalCancel opt\-in applies to every cancel.

<a name="Broker.Close"></a>
### func (\*Broker) [Close](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L297>)

```go
func (b *Broker) Close() error
```

Close releases the broker's resources: it closes the AMQP connection (which requeues any unacked deliveries), stops the background goroutines, and closes every subscriber and fetch channel. Idempotent.

<a name="Broker.FetchJobs"></a>
### func (\*Broker) [FetchJobs](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L997>)

```go
func (b *Broker) FetchJobs(ctx context.Context, keys []bl.ProcessKey) (<-chan bl.Job, error)
```

FetchJobs consumes the quorum queues for the given keys on a dedicated channel with manual ack and bounded prefetch. Deliveries stay unacked until a terminal Report\* verb or ReportSuspended settles them; cancelling ctx closes the channel without acking, so RabbitMQ requeues everything still in flight immediately.

<a name="Broker.RegisterProcesses"></a>
### func (\*Broker) [RegisterProcesses](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L533>)

```go
func (b *Broker) RegisterProcesses(ctx context.Context, workerID string, regs []bl.ProcessRegistration) error
```

<a name="Broker.ReportSuspended"></a>
### func (\*Broker) [ReportSuspended](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L1150>)

```go
func (b *Broker) ReportSuspended(ctx context.Context, instanceID string, resumeAt *time.Time) error
```

ReportSuspended publishes the Suspended lifecycle event, settles (acks) the in\-flight job, and — given a resumeAt — schedules a JobResume through the delay queue.

<a name="Broker.RespondToInputRequest"></a>
### func (\*Broker) [RespondToInputRequest](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L816>)

```go
func (b *Broker) RespondToInputRequest(ctx context.Context, instanceID, requestID string, payload map[string]any) error
```

RespondToInputRequest routes the response as a JobRespondToInput on the instance's process\-key queue. The instance→key mapping comes from this handle's local map, falling back to a replay of the event stream (every event carries the key in its headers); an instance with no visible events surfaces asynchronously as INSTANCE\_NOT\_FOUND.

<a name="Broker.Submit"></a>
### func (\*Broker) [Submit](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L658>)

```go
func (b *Broker) Submit(ctx context.Context, req bl.StartRequest) (string, error)
```

Submit validates the request against the local registry cache (blocking through a cold start — an empty cache — until ctx expires), publishes the Pending lifecycle event and the JobStart, and returns the new instance id.

<a name="Broker.SubscribeToInstance"></a>
### func (\*Broker) [SubscribeToInstance](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L1333>)

```go
func (b *Broker) SubscribeToInstance(ctx context.Context, instanceID string) (<-chan bl.InstanceEvent, error)
```

SubscribeToInstance replays the event stream from the start (bounded by EventRetention) up to a marker this subscriber publishes, collapsing history into the latest lifecycle event plus the terminal Result/Error, then follows live — filtering by instance id client\-side. The channel closes after the final event of a finished instance, or when ctx is cancelled.

```go
func (b *Broker) SubscribeToProcessRegistry(ctx context.Context) (<-chan bl.RegistryUpdate, error)
```

SubscribeToProcessRegistry serves the snapshot (plus sentinel) from the local cache, then live updates, until ctx is cancelled.

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/brokers/rabbitmq/broker.go#L48-L75>)

Config configures New.

```go
type Config struct {
    // URL is the AMQP URI, e.g. "amqp://user:pass@localhost:5672/".
    URL string

    // TLS enables transport encryption; nil means plaintext (development).
    // With TLS set the connection uses amqps.
    TLS *tls.Config

    // ExchangePrefix isolates deployments sharing a server. Default "blkit".
    ExchangePrefix string

    // Cipher enables optional end-to-end payload encryption. Default nil.
    Cipher bl.PayloadCipher

    // RegistrationTTL is how long registrations outlive their last broadcast
    // before the local cache marks the worker lost. Default 90s.
    RegistrationTTL time.Duration

    // InFlightTimeout is accepted for interface symmetry with the other
    // backends but is not used as a timer: RabbitMQ requeues a worker's
    // unacked deliveries the moment its channel or connection closes, so
    // redelivery is immediate rather than timeout-driven. Default 150s.
    InFlightTimeout time.Duration

    // EventRetention bounds the instance-event stream (x-max-age): how long
    // events stay replayable to late subscribers. Default 1h.
    EventRetention time.Duration
}
```
